This selector on `PERSISTED_REQUESTS` returns a filtered array of full `AnyRequest` objects. Each request carries large nested payloads (`optimisticData`, `successData`, `failureData`, `finallyData`, etc.), so Onyx's `deepEqual` on this array runs a deep comparison over every field of every matching request on every queue mutation. This is the "filters/maps a collection into an array — deepEqual on every item" case the rule flags.

Project each request down to only the fields consumed downstream (`command` and the report ID) so the compared output is small:

```ts
const [queuedSpendRequests] = useOnyx(ONYXKEYS.PERSISTED_REQUESTS, {
    selector: (requests) =>
        (requests ?? [])
            .filter((r) => !!r?.command && (YOUR_SPEND_APPROVAL_COMMANDS.has(r.command) || YOUR_SPEND_PAYMENT_COMMANDS.has(r.command)))
            .map((r) => ({command: r.command, reportID: r.data?.reportID ?? r.data?.iouReportID})),
});
```

(and adjust `getYourSpendPendingBuckets` to read the projected shape).

This selector extracts a large sub-property (`pendingChatMembers`, an unbounded `PendingChatMember[]` array) rather than narrowing to a small result. With a selector, Onyx runs `deepEqual` on the selector output to decide whether to re-render, and `deepEqual` over an entire array is compared element-by-element on every `REPORT_METADATA` update — the cost scales with the number of members with no re-render savings versus just reading the field directly.

Since the two call sites only need the array to feed `getGroupChatName`, consider subscribing to the single-item key without a selector and accessing the field inline in each page, e.g.:

```tsx

```

This relies on Onyx's cheap `shallowEqual` on the raw reference instead of an `deepEqual` over the whole array.

`createWorkspaceListPoliciesSelector` subscribes to the entire `POLICY` collection and returns `WorkspaceListPolicy[]` — an array with one mapped object (≈11 fields plus nested `nonMemberDetails` and `errors`) per visible policy. Because a `selector` is supplied, Onyx runs `deepEqual` on this output on every write to any policy, and that comparison cost scales with the number of workspaces. This matches PERF-11's explicit anti-pattern: "Selector filters/maps a collection into an array — the output is still large, `deepEqual` still expensive." The selector reduces each item's depth but not the array's size, so the `deepEqual` savings the selector is meant to provide are largely cancelled out.

Consider subscribing without a selector and shaping the data inline so Onyx falls back to the much cheaper `shallowEqual`:

```tsx
// In WorkspacesListPage.tsx
const [policies] = useOnyx(ONYXKEYS.COLLECTION.POLICY);
const workspaceListPolicies = buildWorkspaceListPolicies(policies, session?.email); // plain function, no selector
```

If a selector must stay, ensure its output is reduced to a small/primitive result (e.g. a count or boolean) rather than a full per-policy array.

This change replaces a narrow single-key subscription (`${ONYXKEYS.COLLECTION.TRANSACTION_VIOLATIONS}${transactionID}`) with a subscription to the entire `TRANSACTION_VIOLATIONS` collection without a selector. This widens render scope and reintroduces unnecessary re-renders that the previous per-key subscription avoided.

Keep the narrow subscription for rendering and only read the full collection where you actually need to pass it to `mergeDuplicates`/`resolveDuplicates`. For example, retain the original key-scoped subscription:

```tsx
const [transactionViolations] = useOnyx(`${ONYXKEYS.COLLECTION.TRANSACTION_VIOLATIONS}${getNonEmptyStringOnyxID(transactionID)}`);
```

If the full collection is required only inside the merge/resolve callbacks, read it there (or via a selector that returns just the needed slice) rather than subscribing the whole component to the entire collection.

The component will re-render whenever **any** report in the collection changes, even though `allReports` is only consumed inside the `onSelectWorkspace` callback. Other files in this same PR correctly use a selector to narrow down to a single report (e.g., `selector: (reports) => getPolicyExpenseChat(accountID, policyID, reports ?? {})`). Since `policy?.id` here comes from the callback parameter and is not known at render time, consider one of these approaches:
